annotation.title_clean: Evaluating the Impact of a Personal Data Communication Policy in Human-Robot Interactions
annotation.title_en: Evaluating the Impact of a Personal Data Communication Policy in Human-Robot Interactions
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Riches, L.; Koay, K.L.; Holthaus, P.
annotation.summary_en: Empirical HRI study testing a communication policy for companion robots that adapts how personal data is conveyed (aloud, choice, or sent to phone) by data sensitivity. A hybrid online/in-person study with a third party present found the policy reduced perceived exposure and increased trust versus no policy.
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes a three-tier communication policy: low-concern said aloud, medium-concern asks user, high-concern sent to phone.
Experimental policy: 68% happy and 78% felt data safe, versus 81% and 85% disagreeing under control.
Participants' trust was driven by consent requests and not voicing sensitive data aloud.
Policy at the communication layer preserves personalisation while limiting personal data exposure.
